text:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: Pager: spike of 401 responses from edge cluster eu-west-1, rate ~4k/min. Affected route: /v1/infer. Sample logs below.

pagerbot: ```
2026-03-15T12:04:22Z eu-west-1 edge-01 401 GET /v1/infer "Authorization: Bearer <token>" x-forwarded-for: 54.36.12.7
2026-03-15T12:04:22Z eu-west-1 edge-03 401 POST /v1/infer "Authorization: Bearer <token>" x-forwarded-for: 54.36.12.9
... (repeated)
```

oliver_sre: Seen it, joining. :eyes: first pass: looks like a burst of invalid tokens, not 5xx. Could be a credential spray or log replayer.

mira_sec: @oliver_sre @jamie_ops - please collect a small sample (10) of full headers + proxied IPs and drop to /sec/incidents/1762142468/samples. Do not include full tokens in bucket, mask them.

leo_eng: copying logs now. Will mask tokens with `sed -E 's/(Bearer) [A-Za-z0-9\-_.]+/\1 <redacted>/'` and upload.

jamie_ops: Quick note — can we isolate eu-west-1 edge pool? I'm ok with temporarily routing to fallback region if this affects customers. Need ops sign-off.

oliver_sre: @jamie_ops do a soft-cordon on edge nodes serving the infer route, preserve healthchecks. I'll update routing policy to failover to eu-central if threshold > 1000 rps per node.

leo_eng: Uploaded sample to /sec/incidents/1762142468/samples/sample-1.txt (masked). Also included a 30s pcap of incoming IPs.

mira_sec: Thanks. Looking at IPs: bulk from a handful of cloud provider ranges, high entropy bearer strings but same token fragments repeating. Hypothesis: replay of cached logs or an exfil attempt + automated replay.

sarah_cs: Any signs of customer-facing errors? I have a handful of support tickets saying latency & 401s since 12:03 UTC. No data exfil yet reported by customers.

elena_cs: Notified the top 10 customers with heavy traffic through eu-west-1 — they reported degraded experience but no data leakage claims. Preparing standby comms.

mira_sec: Ask: can we confirm whether tokens in logs originated from our env (staging/dev) accidentally uploaded publicly? Search S3 for files containing `Authorization: Bearer` in last 7 days.

jamie_ops: Running quick grep against our internal log buckets now. If anything shows, I'll flag with `tag:exposed` and start key rotation.

oliver_sre: Also check the indexer pipeline — we had a misconfigured debug export last week that could have included headers. @leo_eng were there any exports to external buckets?

leo_eng: There was a one-off indexer export to partner-bucket on 2026-03-08, but headers were supposed to be stripped by the pipeline. I'll audit the export manifest and sanitation logs.

mira_sec: If we confirm any exposure, primary action: rotate impacted service tokens, revoke sessions with short TTL (invalidate session store), and issue WAF rule to block high-rate token patterns. Jamie, can operations run a rolling revoke for tokens issued before 2026-03-15T11:55:00Z?

jamie_ops: Can do. I'll prepare a scoped revocation for service-account tokens and ephemeral keys first; user-facing tokens only if we see confirmed customer impact. ETA ~15m.

oliver_sre: Implemented regional failover policy. eu-west-1 traffic for /v1/infer is now routed to eu-central when error-rate > 30% for 30s. Observability dashboard updated.

mira_sec: @legal we may need to start incident classification. At this point, we have unusual auth attempts and potential log exposure. No confirmed PII leak. Guidance?

legal: Thanks for the ping. Please preserve all raw evidence in dedicated S3 path with restricted ACLs and audit logging enabled. If exposure confirmed, we'll need timeline and affected customer list. I'll standby for formal incident call.

leo_eng: Found a debug bundle uploaded 2026-03-10 to s3://dev-exports/debug-bundle-20260310.tar.gz which includes headers. It was supposed to be scrubbed but the sanitizer failed on a specific log format.

mira_sec: That's a smoking gun. Next steps: 1) Mark that object as sensitive and restrict ACLs. 2) Kick off key rotation for service accounts referenced in the bundle. 3) Start targeted customer outreach draft with @elena_cs.

jamie_ops: ACL updated, bucket access logs enabled. Starting service account key rotation for affected indices now. Will post rotation IDs when complete.

oliver_sre: Implemented temporary WAF rule to throttle requests with `Authorization: Bearer` tokens matching the repeating fragment pattern. Hoping to throttle automated replays without blocking legitimate users.

elena_cs: Drafted customer message, focusing on service degradation and mitigation; holding on confirmation of token exposure before sending anything mentioning credentials.

mira_sec: We've got a containment path. Priority: confirm which tokens in bundle map to active sessions. If matched => revoke. I'll run a quick correlation across token IDs and session store.

leo_eng: Correlation run complete: 42 tokens in bundle match active sessions (mostly test/service tokens). 3 appear to be long-lived service tokens tied to indexer.

jamie_ops: Revoked the 3 long-lived service tokens and rotated their keys. New keys deployed to indexer config. Can we validate that indexer no longer uses old creds?

leo_eng: Confirmed via handshake logs — new tokens in use. Old tokens show no successful auth after rotation.

mira_sec: Good. Next: plan for broader rotation of ephemeral tokens if we see customer impact. For now, limited rotation and monitoring. Schedule incident bridge in 30m for post-mortem and next steps.

elena_cs: I'll prepare comms for the bridge and pre-approve message templates with legal.

legal: Ready to join bridge. If customer PII is confirmed, we'll move to notification plan.

jamie_ops: Ops on-call handoff in 20m: @oliver_sre will take lead for next 2 hours. I'll remain available for key rotations.

oliver_sre: Taking lead. Current status summary pinned to /sec/incidents/1762142468/status.txt. Monitoring for replay resumption; WAF rule in place.

pagerbot: Update: 401 spike down to background levels (~120/min) after WAF throttle and regional failover. Continued monitoring recommended.

mira_sec: Great work team. Post-incident actions: 1) Fix sanitizer pipeline and add unit test for header formats. 2) Rotate any remaining long-lived tokens on cadence. 3) Run audit for any other debug exports last 30 days. Assign owners in bridge.

elena_cs: Noted for customer follow-up. Will await final incident severity classification before outbound.

legal: Preserving evidence path and will request timeline for regulatory reporting if classification requires.

oliver_sre: Bridge in 30 — joining link: https://meet.company/incident/1762142468. Closing slack triage here, continue updates in the bridge and status doc. :white_check_mark:
